cells.gaps: No row sets the tiers in use, and no share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: the minister's count of over 90 clinics reached by data collection (NAM-020, May 2025) has no total and names no system, and the newer NAM-004 and NAM-005 (March 2026) have district entry from paper and clinics on paper, so the newer stands; NAM-015 (2025-09) has four of 20 respondents saying primary facilities upload some data. On the plan, the managers' statement that no health information systems policy exists (NAM-008, published March 2026) stands against the National Digital Health Policy 2026-2036 launched in February 2026 (NAM-018), whose period covers the as-at. The only event inside the twelve months is that launch (NAM-019), not a change in where reports are entered.
cells.note: District officers key the facilities' monthly paper forms into DHIS2 aggregate, which is the stage 3 row. Stage 4 needs entry at the facility by more than half of primary clinics, and the newest facts say clinics still report on paper.

cells.gaps: No row gives primary clinics keeping an electronic record: the minister's five health centres and 18 clinics (NAM-024, May 2025) are sites where the e-Health system's network is operational, with no total of clinics, and the newer rows have paper records in most hospitals and clinics (NAM-011, 2025-09; NAM-023, March 2026). The plan is the National Digital Health Policy 2026-2036 (NAM-021); the eHealth Strategy 2021-2025 of NAM-009 has ended. Finance is the ministry's own budget request of May 2025 (NAM-025), which is for health data and policy support and is not tied to the record system by name; NAM-014 (2025-09) names no budget line. The only owner row, NAM-012, is dated 2011, outside the 36 months; owner:ministry is taken from the text of NAM-009 and NAM-013. The event inside the twelve months is the policy launch (NAM-022); the Katutura and Windhoek Central pilot is a billing module, out of scope.
cells.note: IHCIMS is fully deployed at two hospitals only, Windhoek Central and Oshakati, with paper records in most hospitals and clinics, which is the stage 2 row. Stage 3 needs most T1 and T2 hospitals or primary clinics in some districts, and neither is evidenced; stage 1 fails because two hospitals use the system.
